value: temperature (30 C against a 24 C control) had a significant effect on shoot mortality in plants from the eutrophic Bacoli site (EU), two-way ANOVA F = 10.15, P = 0.01
method: mesocosm with 12 glass aquaria (500 L), four treatments (control, temperature, nutrients, nutrients plus temperature); shoot number counted at the start and end and the net change expressed as a percentage; three-way ANOVA (plants, temperature, nutrients) and, because the plant factor was significant, two-way ANOVA run separately for each site (Table 1)
conditions: EU plants only: plants collected in May 2019 at 7 to 9 m from Bacoli (relatively eutrophic, EU); two fragments of 15 to 20 connected shoots per basket, one EU basket per tank, three aquaria per treatment (aquarium is the experimental unit, n = 3 per treatment, error df 8); one week at 21 C, then warmed 0.5 C per day to 30 C, control 24 C; five weeks; nutrients (nominal 100 uM total nitrogen weekly) crossed with temperature. Same Table 1 row for the oligotrophic Ischia site (OL), held in the same tanks: no significant temperature effect on shoot mortality (F = 1.20, P = 0.31). EU N x T interaction P = 0.08, nutrients P = 0.23. Net shoot change in EU plants: -41.6% under T, -27.9% under NT, -23% under N; OL plants -15.7% (T), -15.6% (NT), -7% (N); most mortality between T2 and T4 (Supplementary Figure 2, not read). The Results sentence 'Temperature was the main factor that affected shoot mortality along the experiment (P < 0.05).' pools both sites from the three-way ANOVA (Supplementary Table 2, not read) and is not used. Relative growth rate: the text says statistical analysis revealed no significant differences between plants and treatments, but Table 1 prints a significant N x T interaction for OL plants (F = 5.05, P = 0.04); RGR temperature P = 0.31 (OL), 0.91 (EU). One warm level only (30 C); the full T0 to T4 schedule is in Figure 1C, not read.
